| # | Element | Meaning | Values | Required | Default |
|---|-------|---------|--------|----------|---------|
| 1 | Package name | The npm package identity used for the git-based install command | `forgent` | yes | — |
| 2 | Package version | A semantic version string tooling (e.g. packaging commands) needs to treat the package as valid | semver string | yes | `0.1.0` |
| 3 | Distribution file allowlist | The exact set of paths shipped to anyone installing the package — everything else in the source repo is excluded | `bin`, `src`, `scripts`, `core`, `domains`, `.agents`, `README.md`, `LICENSE`, the end-user documentation subset (`docs/how-to`, `docs/explanation`, and `docs/enduser-docs-index.json`), plus `packages/convention/contracts/convention.rules.v1.json`, which installed doctor needs to interpret per-rule cutoffs without duplicating native rule data, and `packages/seat-binding/contracts/seat-binding.tier-ladder.v1.json`, the tier names the runner config loader accepts, read from the same file the Seat Binding crate embeds | yes | — |
| 4 | CLI entry points | The commands exposed once installed | `fgos` → runs `bin/fgos.mjs`; `fgos-runner` → runs `bin/fgos-runner.mjs` (the autonomous-loop runner, see spec Runner) | yes | — |
| 4b | Claude Code plugin skill set | `plugins/fgOS/skills/` — the Claude Code plugin's own skill bundle, distributed via the Claude Code plugin marketplace mechanism (a separate distribution channel from the npm-installed `fgos`/`fgos-runner` CLI above). Ships two layers: hand-authored CLI-wrapper skills (`cook`, `discover`, `pick`, `submit`, ...) and mirrored `fgos-*` dev-skills plus `_shared/` for plugin-only consumers. Dev-skills are authored in `core/skills/` or `domains/*/skills/`; run `npm run build:skills` in the fgOS source repo to assemble `.agents/skills/`, generate `.claude/skills/` thin wrappers and references, and mirror dev-skills/shared fragments into the plugin. Plugin mirrors stay byte-identical to `.agents/skills/`, while Claude `SKILL.md` files are thin redirects with byte-identical frontmatter (`test/skills/fgos-mirror.test.mjs`). Assembled Markdown carries a generated-from source header. Do not hand-edit `.agents`, generated `.claude` files, or plugin mirrors; hand-authored CLI-wrapper skills remain sources. `plugin-dev-skills-packaged` (doctor check, row 7 below) detects missing or stale plugin mirrors | mirrored dev-skills + shared fragments + hand-authored CLI-wrapper skills | yes (the mirrors let plugin-only consumers dispatch dev-skills without a source checkout) | — |
| 5 | Dev checkout shell helper | An opt-in file, sourced from a contributor's own shell profile, exposing the same two CLI entry points from inside a checkout of the source repository — no install, no package fetch | one file, both commands | no (contributor's own choice) | not sourced automatically anywhere |
| 5b | Global config file | `~/.fgos/config.json` — same schema as the project-local shared config file, initialized/kept current by `fgos setup` (tsk-1ri) the same way it already handles the project-local file; project always wins any key present in both (`mergeWithGlobalConfig`, `src/config/global-config.mjs`) | one file, home-dir-relative | no (optional; a missing file is not an error, resolves to `{}`) | not created by anything except `fgos setup` |
| 5c | Machine backend registry file | `~/.fgos/confinement-backends.json` (overridable via `FGOS_CONFINEMENT_BACKEND_REGISTRY_PATH`) — machine-local backend registry declaring confinement backends (e.g. `bwrap`, container) available on the host (`confinement-backend-registry.v1`); managed by `fgos doctor --fix` (not project-over-global merge), trust store for security isolation drivers | one file, machine-local path | no (optional; bootstrap creates default bwrap backend on demand) | `~/.fgos/confinement-backends.json` |
| 5d | Provider-capacity runtime state | `~/.fgos/runtime/provider-capacity/state.json` — machine-local selected-account lease/quarantine state for provider-capacity rotation. Intentionally host-global only (never project-overridden) so multiple projects sharing provider accounts coordinate concurrency and rate limits safely without starvation. It is never packaged, never committed, and never repaired by `doctor`; `fgos dispatch inspect --provider-capacity` and the `provider-capacity-state` doctor check report it, while manual clear goes through `fgos dispatch reconcile provider-capacity clear-quarantine ...`. An account locked for a dead login is also unlocked by one real call when a dispatch would otherwise find no usable account (the lazy-probe unlock rule, now in `docs/specs/runner.md`). Its locks are holder-lock kernel locks under the machine lock root (row 5g): `provider-state` guards this file, and `provider-account/<provider>/<account>` guards one account while a renewal or unlock probe runs through it, held until that call and every process it started have exited. The same directory holds `account-locks/<provider>/<account>/`: copies of a login renewed elsewhere and waiting to be applied, a scratch home while a renewal runs, and the renewal failure cooldown; it is created only when a renewal or write-back runs and holds no credential outside those copies. | one runtime directory, home-dir-relative | no (created only when a provider account lease/quarantine/write occurs) | absent/inactive |
| 5e | Confinement attestation store state | `~/.local/state/fgos/attestations/` (or `$XDG_STATE_HOME/fgos/attestations`, overridable via `FGOS_CONFINEMENT_ATTESTATION_STORE_PATH`) — host-global security attestation records. Intentionally host-global only (outside all agent write grants) so confined agents can never tamper with their own audit trails, preserving immutable attestation integrity across projects. | one directory, machine-local path | no (created on first confined dispatch attestation) | absent/inactive |
| 5f | Workspace customization folder | `fgos/` at the project root: tracked in the project's own git, written once as a skeleton at onboarding and never edited by fgOS afterwards. Holds the customer's own agent definitions (`fgos/agents/<name>.yaml`), which win over a definition of the same name in the installed set (RUL13 (customer customization lives in one tracked workspace folder)). Read by `--seats @name` (runner decision 0057); the `fgctl init` skeleton is not built yet | directory | no | absent — the installed set alone applies |
| 5g | Lock directories | `<lockRoot>` = `<stateRoot>/locks` (machine-scope lock files: `full-suite`, `provider-account/<provider>/<account>`, `provider-state`, `install`) and `<fgosDir>/locks` (repo-scope lock files: `gateway`, `runner`, `sessions`, `reconcile`, `main-checkout`, `worktree-admin`, `merge-slot--<encodeURIComponent(ref)>` per target ref, `state.hot` and `state.reclaim.lock`, `porting-events.hot` and `porting-events.reclaim.lock` (the state store's hot mutex: the `.hot` record is not a kernel lock file, only the `.reclaim.lock` file is), `activation`, `observe`, and `dispatch-cwd--<dev>-<ino>` keyed by the dispatch directory's identity after realpath; the run locks live in their run: `<workflowRunDir>/locks/advance.lock`, `<runDir>/locks/recovery.lock`), both created by `fgos setup` (the machine root with mode 0700); `stateRoot` is the single resolution of `docs/platform/holder-lock/spec.md` §11 (`FGOS_STATE_ROOT` pinned by the host, else `FGOS_STATE_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME/fgos`, `HOME/.local/state/fgos`). There is no lock config key: the wait for the processes of a dead previous holder to exit after they are terminated is fixed at 2000 ms. Lock files are never packaged, committed or repaired; `lock-kernel-semantics`, `lock-borrow-vectors` and `lock-holders` report them (row 7) | two directories | no (created by setup) | none |
| 5h | Terminal-control directory and the `terminal` config key | `<stateRoot>/terminal` (one subdirectory per driver; allocation records and their markers, a cache of what the port opened: deleting it never closes a pane because nobody closes a pane that has no record), created with mode 0700, together with every directory under it, by the allocation store on first use (there is no setup fix for it). One config key, `terminal` (`registerConfigDefault({id: 'terminal', key: 'terminal', shape: {allocationGraceMs: 60000, retainFailedPaneMs: null, layout: {policy: 'measured-split', minCols: 80, minRows: 20, maxPanesPerTab: 8}}})`); `docs/platform/terminal-control/spec.md` §9 gives each number's source. Project over global over default; the merge adds a missing key only. No new environment variable (`FGOS_HERDR_ANCHOR_PANE` stays, as the input of `attach`). Checked 2026-10-18: the release active in the forgentX, mdview and mcp-skill-hub workspaces (one digest) accepts a `terminal` section in the global and in the project config, so the key is written like `lock`; had it refused unknown keys, setup would have written it to the project config only until all three workspaces ran the new release. | `<stateRoot>/terminal` present / absent; config key present / absent | yes (computed, not stored) | — |
| 6 | Config staleness | Whether a config file (project-local or global — same computation, tsk-1ri) already has every setting the current default schema defines | up to date / missing one or more default settings | yes (computed, not stored) | — |
| 7 | Doctor check | One named diagnostic `fgos doctor` reports on | not a fixed list — an extensible registry (`src/setup/registrations.mjs`'s `registerCheck`); a check registration and a config-default registration are independent, never a forced pairing — a module may register only a check, only a config-default, or both. Today's registered checks: `convention-conformance`, `identity-project-id` (this repository carries one project id in the tracked file `.fgos/project.json`, asked through `fgos identity project --json`; absent only warns and there is no fix, because a fix on every machine would mint one id per clone: `fgos identity project --init` runs once on one machine, the file is committed and the others pull it; an unreadable or invalid file fails), `node-version-and-git`, `cli-version-visible` (tsk-2ej), `shell-integration-sourced`, `project-fgos-launcher` (a release install has one fgos launcher on PATH that runs each project's own activated fgos, see RUL17 (one fgos on PATH runs each project's own activated fgos)), `config-not-stale`, `main-checkout-hook-wired`, `tool-registry-configured`, `work-classification-vocabulary`, `work-step-vocabulary` (tsk-64h), `domain-workflow-operations-coverage`, `root-drift`, `delivered-not-on-trunk` (tsk-1l9), `config-awareness`, `provider-capacity-state` (reports account lease/quarantine state and never auto-clears), `credential-copies-retained` (login copies still pending for a renewal after a day, and private homes held after repeated staging failures, counted by provider/account and age; read-only, a held home fails, copies waiting for a renewal only warn, and, when the machine-global provider inventory was read, copies of any age in a store directory the account's login store layout no longer reads fail, naming the directory for hand recovery (when the global config cannot be read or is refused by the validator the check fails, says the layout was not checked with the reason, lists copies at any age and promises nothing about a dispatch); interrupted stagings (pending/.tmp-*) are reported too once their writer is gone and they have sat for ten minutes, and the over-limit line names the store; kept homes under a registered backend's temp and private-home roots are scanned, which the orphan reaper check does not do, and one there counts as held at once because nothing retries it; the check itself never deletes and never prints a value), `lock-kernel-semantics` (for the workspace lock directory and the machine lock root: the holder-lock driver's guarantee through the in-process door, then a two-process probe on that same mount, a description locked here and handed to a child must read held while the child lives and free once it died; prints driver, exclusion, borrow and holders levels, then the state root with its source and the fixed 2000 ms kill wait; kernel with a green probe passes, a missing directory warns until setup creates it, a guarantee of unsupported (a platform with no driver), a network filesystem none, an unresolved state root and an unreachable door fail by name; on Windows the probe runs over a lock-hold helper and the message shows lockfileex), `lock-borrow-vectors` (runs the host's lock-borrow-vectors route: a lock description borrowed by a git child must not leak to any background process git starts; any red vector or a red sibling check fails, unavailable fails, since activation refuses the same result and there is no run-time switch that disables borrowing; runs on Windows with its own pid-handle assertion), `lock-holders` (for every existing lock file of the locks this release cut over, including the main checkout, merge slot and worktree-admin files, the holders the kernel lists: a holder whose origin is foreign (neither a fgOS process, by the host's state-root pin or a fgOS payload in its argv, nor a borrowed child of that lock) warns with pid and cmdline; a predecessor record next to a lock file naming a domain that is not empty, an unknown record version or a Windows job the host does not judge empty warns with the domain and the reason; the state and porting-events hot records of the workspace, under .fgos/locks, warn with the path and the fence command of the lock verb when a record does not parse or its holder cannot be placed for more than five minutes (absent, alive or dead holders pass; no automatic fix, because a person confirms the holder is gone); holders that cannot be listed are informational), `dependencies-installed`, `gate-bypass-configured`, `claude-plugin-marketplace`, `plugin-skill-cli-reachable`, `plugin-dev-skills-packaged` (tsk-32b), `changelog-unreleased-stale`, `herdr-launcher-configured`, `herdr-web-dashboard-configured` (tsk-48w), `enduser-docs-index-stale` (tsk-1m0), `invariant-checks-configured` (tsk-516), `invocation-git-write-grants` (warns when an invocation or executor still grants a git add or git commit tool; the runner commits, workers only edit files; read-only, never rewrites user config), `worktree-setup-configured` (a present worktreeSetup section is a list of non-empty shell commands every runner-created worktree runs after its dependency install; never executes them), `events-jsonl-not-truncated` (tsk-cgg), `worker-slots-ceiling-usable` (tsk-1oz), `gateway-token-configured` (tsk-4r1), `readme-install-tag-exists` (tsk-2t8), `iron-law-configured` (tsk-1y6-1), `leaf-notify-drift` (tsk-1el), `task-specs-resolve` (tsk-2t9c), `agent-claims-resolve` (tsk-2t9c), `agent-type-names-unique` (tsk-397-12; names unique within each tier fgos/agents, domains/*/agents, core/agents, a higher tier replaces a lower one whole, the fgos/agents files checked for shape), `domain-registry-compiled` (every domain's compiled.json file under domains — the precompiled form of the registry and workflow YAML the Work lifecycle reads, regenerated by the build:domains npm script; the check reports a missing, unreadable or stale file and domain YAML that cannot be parsed, and a drift test keeps it equal to the YAML), `dispatch-decide-hook-wired` (tsk-60f; also requires the AskUserQuestion decision-question hook), `codex-hook-wired`, `agy-hook-wired`, `omp-hook-wired`, `pi-hook-wired`, `decision-index-stale` (tsk-1lv-2/tsk-1lv), `advise-execute-capabilities-configured` (tsk-2uf-3), `workflow-capabilities-configured` (every capability a core/domain Workflow unit names resolves in runner.capabilities by exact name or bare verb, the way bind() looks it up, and fails when it does not; one that resolves but has no "prefer" pool on either name is reported as a warning because bind() refuses its unit headless; fgos setup registers every shipped Workflow's capabilities as description-only defaults, so a fresh project starts with that warning, and never overwrites a project's own entry), `capability-serves-valid` (I19: every runner.capabilities entry's serves attribute set is well-formed, no two entries declare the identical set, and the review slot is present), `agy-permissions-configured` (tsk-1xm), `agy-sub-homes-configured`, `bwrap-available`, `curl-available` (curl runs, because fgctl init downloads a release through it; confirms legacy definition fixtures retired), `operation-prompt-templates-valid` (Phase 03 I04: every discoverable operation prompt template validates against bounded variables and schema), `coordination-example-requests-valid` (Step 08 Phase 07 R3: published fgos coordination run example request files validate against the same schema boundary the CLI itself enforces, and resolve every referenced protocolRef), `terminal-control` (the terminal-control driver answers through the internal route: driver, declared capabilities and the herdr server incarnation are printed, then the terminal section after the merge with each value and its source; a missing herdr only warns, a missing layout.geometry capability is information, and a bad FGOS_HERDR_ANCHOR_PANE fails, as does a terminal value the core or the grace rules refuse, by name), `terminal-allocations` (slots past terminal.allocationGraceMs that never launched and retained panes past their time, from the route's reconcile-scan, each with its pane id; reports only, closes nothing), `trust-store-readable`, `non-claude-trust-stores-readable` (Phase 07 herdr-trust-supervisor R3: every executor or invocation declaring a codex-toml or agy/agy-json trustStore reads from a store that is actually readable, using the same reader the live dispatch will use), `confined-pane-accounts` (every confined herdr invocation that binds a private home has an account in the machine-global provider account inventory whose credential files exist, so its pane starts logged in; sourceBindings.sourceContent:
- **Blocked when:** never — running `fgos setup` always attempts its work;
  a shell profile that does not exist is simply skipped rather than
  refused.
- **What changes:** for every shell profile the caller actually has (bash's
  and/or zsh's, whichever exist), the shell helper's source line is added
  if not already present — never duplicated on a repeat run. The local
  project config file is also brought up to date: any setting present in
  the current default schema but missing from the caller's file is added,
  without ever changing a setting the caller already customized; a config
  file that already has every current default is left untouched. The same
  fill-missing-only treatment is applied to the **global** config file
  (`~/.fgos/config.json`, tsk-1ri) — `fgos setup` initializes it with the
  same default schema the project-local file gets, or fills in any missing
  key, every time it runs, regardless of which project it's run from;
  a value the caller already customized at the global level is never
  overwritten. The lock directories of row 5g are created when missing:
  `<lockRoot>` and `<fgosDir>/locks`, both mode 0700, an existing one tightened to it (the `lock-dirs` fix);
  the `terminal` section of row 5h is one of the defaults the
  fill-missing-only merge adds; `<stateRoot>/terminal` is not set up here: the
  terminal allocation store creates it with mode 0700 on first use.
- **Side effects:** the caller's own shell profile file(s), local project
  config file, global config file (`~/.fgos/config.json`), and the two lock
  directories may be created or modified; nothing outside the caller's own
  environment is touched, and no network access happens.
- **Afterwards:** the caller sees exactly what changed — which profile
  file(s) gained the source line (or already had it), which project config
  settings were newly added (or that none were needed), and which global
  config settings were newly added (or that none were needed, or that the
  global file was just created). Nothing is done silently; running `fgos
  setup` again when everything is already current reports that plainly,
  without repeating any change.

placement.content: - **RUL107 (a third-party crate that a component's contract rests on is pinned exactly and has an upgrade record and acceptance tests; 2026-10-23).** Such a crate (the YAML parser under `fgos-yaml-doc`, the JSON Schema validator under `fgos-config`) is pinned with `=` in the root `[workspace.dependencies]`, never a range; the package that relies on it carries an `upgrade-record.md` (what was read, transitive crates, audit coverage, deny result, known defects with their guards and upstream links, bump procedure, owner sign-off) and acceptance tests that fail when a bump changes a behavior the contract depends on, including one test per known defect that fails when upstream fixes it. A bump lands only when those tests pass and the record is updated. Backlog item p-3c9e7a15 extends this to every dependency. Records: `packages/yaml-doc/upgrade-record.md`, `packages/config/upgrade-record.md`.

- **RUL108 (every YAML parse goes through the native door: one Rust parser behind `src/util/yaml.mjs`; supersedes RUL101; 2026-10-23).** `fgos-yaml-doc` (parser `saphyr-parser` =0.2.2, pinned and vendored under RUL107 (a third-party crate under a component contract is pinned exactly with an upgrade record and acceptance tests)) is the only YAML parser. `parseYaml(text, { filename })` keeps its signature and calls the addon's `yaml` namespace with the `tool` profile; objects reach JavaScript from JSON text, so a `__proto__` key stays an own key; a Rust panic becomes the named refusal `yaml-internal-error` and never aborts Node. There is no JavaScript fallback: a process that cannot load the addon fails every YAML read with the door's named error (`git-addon-unavailable` or `git-addon-not-shipped`). `package.json#dependencies` stays empty. `test/architecture.test.mjs` fails on any YAML library import anywhere, the door included; `.github/cargo-deny.toml` bans the other Rust YAML crates. Authority for what YAML means: `docs/platform/yaml-document/spec.md`.

sourceBindings.sourceContent:
- **2026-10-23 — Terminal setup loses a row and a fix.** The doctor row `terminal-config` is part of `terminal-control`, and the `terminal-dir` fix is gone: the allocation store creates `<stateRoot>/terminal` and everything under it with mode 0700 itself, so a repair that only recreated what the owner of the directory already creates was a second door. Source: `docs/platform/terminal-control/spec.md` §15 and the T2 arbitration `plans/reports/council-261023-0402-harden-t2-arbitration.md`.
- **2026-10-23 — Every YAML parse goes through the native door (RUL108 (every YAML parse goes through the native door: one Rust parser behind src/util/yaml.mjs); supersedes RUL101 (fgOS has no npm runtime dependency; every YAML parse goes through one vendored js-yaml 5.4.3 behind src/util/yaml.mjs)).** Before this, a vendored, hash-pinned js-yaml 5.4.3 bundle was the Node parser because a bare checkout had no `npm install`, while the Rust side already read YAML through `fgos-yaml-doc`: two authorities for what YAML means. Decision: the one-door rule of RUL101 (every YAML parse goes through one vendored js-yaml) stays and the implementation behind the door becomes Rust, as the YAML Document spec (section 10) signed on 2026-10-22 says. `src/util/third-party/js-yaml.mjs` and its hash test are deleted in the same change; the upgrade-procedure paragraph of RUL101 (every YAML parse goes through one vendored js-yaml) no longer applies (the parser's own record is `packages/yaml-doc/upgrade-record.md`, RUL107 (a third-party crate under a component contract is pinned exactly with an upgrade record and acceptance tests)). Consequence, stated plainly: a process that cannot load the addon (a bare checkout without a staged addon, a channel that does not ship it) fails every YAML read with the door's named error; scripts that read YAML from a checkout stage the addon first (`ensureAddonForScript`), and a focused `node --test` needs the staged environment `npm test` builds. Evidence: the 136 golden cases of `packages/yaml-doc/contracts/fixtures/parse.v1.json` (every case of the old Node test lives there); a parity run of the old door against the new over 1414 tracked YAML and frontmatter documents found 1396 equal, 18 rejected by both, 0 different; `test/util/yaml.test.mjs` is the one Node wiring proof. Rejected: keeping js-yaml beside the crate (two authorities), a JSON projection plus a spawned process (owner 2026-10-22: 3 to 40 ms per call against 12 microseconds). Reversal condition: if the addon cannot be loaded on a channel the product must support, the fix is to ship the addon there, never a JavaScript parser.

- **2026-10-12 — `fgctl init` downloads by default (RUL15 (fgctl init downloads a checksum-verified release when no source is given)).** Before this, a plain `fgctl init` in a project with no pin failed with "`--from <source>` is required", so a first install meant downloading the release tarball by hand. Owner decision: no source and no pin means the latest GitHub release; `FGCTL_VERSION` selects an exact tag; `FGCTL_FROM` and `--from` select a non-release build; checksum verification is mandatory; the transport is the system `curl` rather than a new HTTP crate (same behavior and override as `install.sh`, no TLS stack to carry in `fgctl`). Prior art: `fgctl init --from` (the release-asset door, kept unchanged and now equivalent to `FGCTL_FROM`), `install.sh`'s `FGCTL_VERSION`/`FGCTL_ASSET_BASE_URL`/`FGCTL_TARGET` (reused, not redefined). Same day, follow-up: the pin now records the tag, so a pinned workspace whose release is not staged on this machine downloads it instead of needing a source; only a digest-only legacy pin still needs `FGCTL_FROM`/`FGCTL_VERSION`/`--from`, because a digest names no download. Follow-up (2026-10-14): `fgctl upgrade` uses the same verified download pipeline (`--from` > `FGCTL_FROM` > `FGCTL_VERSION` > latest GitHub release) and records the downloaded tag in `.fgos/distribution.json`, so an upgraded project's pin keeps a downloadable `releaseVersion` for teammates instead of reverting to digest-only.
- **2026-10-13 — Windows is a native release target (RUL16 (Windows is a native release target: same assets, an installer and launchers that need no POSIX shell)).** Owner decision: the level is "native, complete" (PowerShell and `cmd.exe`, no Git Bash, no WSL), with `tar.gz` kept as the single archive format and macOS left out of scope. Prior art, reused: the Windows CI hardening track made the Rust workspace build and the release-tree staging work on Windows (the `fgos.exe` entry, colon-free release store directory names, drive-letter-safe archive validation), and an earlier change wrote `.cmd` launchers on Windows that ran the `sh` shims through a `sh` on `PATH`; that required Git for Windows, so it is replaced by launchers that read `activation.json` themselves. Missing before: a Windows release asset, `install.ps1`, a Windows consumer proof, and any check that the launchers exist. Also in this change: the Linux asset moves from `ubuntu-latest` (binaries then needed glibc 2.39 and printed a loader warning on Ubuntu 22.04, glibc 2.35) to `ubuntu-22.04`, with a CI gate on the glibc symbol versions.
- **2026-10-16 — fgOS has no npm runtime dependency; YAML is read through one vendored parser (RUL101 (fgOS has no npm runtime dependency; every YAML parse goes through one vendored js-yaml 5.4.3 behind src/util/yaml.mjs)).** **Superseded on 2026-10-23 by RUL108 (every YAML parse goes through the native door): the one-door rule stays, the parser behind the door is now the Rust crate, the vendored file, its hash test and the upgrade procedure below are gone; the text below is kept as history.** Before this, `yaml` was the one production dependency. An installed release carried it (the release builder stages declared production dependencies), but a checkout, linked worktree or unpacked copy without `npm install` did not, so every module importing it failed to load there, and the doctor and setup paths grew their own YAML readers and "not evaluated" branches to keep loading. Decision: `package.json#dependencies` stays empty; the only YAML parser is `src/util/third-party/js-yaml.mjs`, the ESM bundle from the js-yaml 5.4.3 tarball, unmodified except a header and the dropped source-map comment line, and every parse goes through `src/util/yaml.mjs` (`parseYaml(text, { filename })`: zero documents give `null`, more than one throws, `maxAliases` 100, js-yaml's default core schema). An architecture test fails on any other import of `yaml`, `js-yaml` or the third-party file. Rejected: keeping `yaml` and making doctor tolerate its absence (what the workarounds did, and the cause of the divergence); a hand-rolled parser (a second authority for what YAML means); `vendor/` or `dist/` as the location (the repository's scout-block hook refuses those path segments, so agents could not read or review the file); 5.4.2 (a block-indentation mis-parse fixed in 5.4.3) and 5.5.0 (one day old at the time). Readers that used to skip silently now report a parse failure as a named problem with file, line and column; pinned persona text that the strict parser rejects renders through a private legacy projection so older runs resume with the same text (its removal is tracked in the backlog). Evidence: commits `8ef1baf1c` (door and vendored file), `838b044e5` (call sites), `b75c01a3f` (release and dev-host staging), `6013ca389` (dependency dropped), `f96eece77`, `b7eeb4bb6` and `26b3338a7` (readers use the parser), `f705b9c8c` (doctor checks `compiled.json`); a parity run of the old parser against the door over every tracked YAML and frontmatter document found 828 documents, 0 differences, 13 rejected by both; a cold `fgos` start costs 2 to 3 ms more (97 to 99 ms for `version`, 109 to 110 ms for `dispatch decide`); the full suite ran 7850 tests with 0 failures with release binaries present; `test/util/yaml.test.mjs` pins the vendored bytes by hash. Kept on their own paths: `src/report/frontmatter.mjs` pairs `parseFrontmatter` with `renderFrontmatter` over a deliberately flat schema, so replacing only the parser would make the pair asymmetric; `distill.mjs` carries a minimal YAML reader because portable skills ship without `src/`; `domains/*/compiled.json` stays a generated projection because parsing domain YAML at import would put every verb, hook and `doctor` at the mercy of one YAML typo (doctor now checks its freshness instead). Upgrade procedure: in an empty scratch directory run `npm pack js-yaml@<version> --ignore-scripts`; compare the tarball's sha512 with `npm view js-yaml@<version> dist.integrity`; extract the `.mjs` bundle from the tarball without executing anything in it (build the path so the hook-refused segment does not appear in the command); confirm it has no import or require; diff it against the current bundle and read every changed line; re-run the parity comparison against the previous parser over the tracked YAML; replace the third-party file with the new bundle under a fresh header (source, version, integrity, license, hash); update the hash constant in `test/util/yaml.test.mjs`. js-yaml advisories are watched through the backlog, since `npm audit` no longer covers the file.
- **2026-10-17 — Instruction composition belongs to the Agent Context Engine; packaging-distribution delivers (RUL102 (one owner for composing agent instructions: the Agent Context Engine composes and selects rules, packaging-distribution only discovers, installs, renders per host and repairs)).** Before this, two documents gave the same authority to two components: `docs/platform/packaging-distribution/contracts/instruction-composition-and-projection.md` §2 named packaging-distribution owner of the composition engine and registry shape, while `docs/platform/proposals/documentation-system-unification.md` §4.7.2-4.7.3 put the Instruction Composer in the Agent Context Engine and said packaging-distribution "does not decide semantic composition". Left as is, a future Agent Context Engine would be built beside `src/setup/instruction-composition.mjs`, giving two composers and two orderings of the same rules. Owner decision: composing and selecting rules (kind order, override, conflict, per-task selection, per-host budget, progressive disclosure) has one owner, the Agent Context Engine; packaging-distribution keeps delivery (source discovery and install, per-host render adapters, projection ledger, doctor repair). Two delivery moments follow: static delivery, where packaging-distribution asks the engine for each host's effective set when sources change or at setup/install/upgrade and renders it to files; and per-task delivery, where the runner asks the engine for a context packet that goes into the worker brief, with no file written. The engine knows no host or file. Rejected: packaging-distribution keeping composition and also absorbing budgets and per-task selection (it would grow a content-deciding role inside an install/delivery component). Weight guard: no new component now; the existing code in `src/setup/instruction-registry.mjs` and `src/setup/instruction-composition.mjs` is the engine's seed and moves to its own module only when the first budget/tiering slice lands, in the same change, never kept in two places. Evidence and reasoning: `plans/reports/research-261016-1118-agent-code-quality-guardrails.md` sections 2d and 6.

- `docs/backlog.md` — product backlog (PBI rows, scribing-owned)
- `docs/architecture-map.md` — bản chuẩn kiến trúc (v0.2, record ADR0010 (bản đồ kiến trúc là bản chuẩn)): 5 tầng + 2 lớp phủ, sổ component + sổ contract (CTR001–CTR009), nghi thức thẻ-căn-cước-trước-code
- `docs/work-item-lifecycle-vision.md` — tầm nhìn nền tảng: chu trình sống của work-item (mixed-autonomy, base-workflow + domain-extension); khung cho các PBI STR14-STR18
- `docs/platform/packaging-distribution/README.md` — portal hiện hành cho packaging/distribution: `fgctl` bootstrap/init/repair/upgrade, workspace activation, doctor/fix readiness, legacy Node compatibility, skill/instruction projections. Khi mục này mâu thuẫn với `docs/specs/distribution.md`, đọc portal + implementation-alignment trước; `docs/specs/distribution.md` hiện là legacy/generated-curated source trong lúc migration.
- `docs/distribution-vision.md` — tầm nhìn nền tảng lịch sử: cài đặt/setup/doctor ổn định + tái dùng được (không cần clone, global/project không xung đột — project ghi đè global, doctor/setup tự fix hạ tầng + merge config thiếu, module mới tự đăng ký năng lực config, CI như một phần của setup); đã được promote/supersede từng phần vào `docs/platform/packaging-distribution/vision.md`.
- `docs/specs/` — state layer: area spec + system-overview + bản đồ này
- `docs/routing-handoff-contract.md` — hợp đồng handoff agent↔agent + ranh giới tin cậy
- `docs/io-contract.md` — hợp đồng giao tiếp VÀO/RA của cửa CLI + bề mặt stdout `fgos-runner` (str46-io-contract): danh tính `writer`/`role`, envelope `fgos.v1` + ngoại lệ có lý do, exit-code một nguồn, sổ verb (`touchesState`/`externalEffect`/`paginated`/`multiValueFormat`), version token, ranh giới ngoài (STR38/STR48/STR83)
- `docs/coexistence.md` — doctrine chạy cạnh một harness agent khác (record ADR0009 (chống giao thoa lúc cài — fgOS khi cài không giao thoa tiến trình với harness khác)): lãnh địa, một-nhạc-trưởng-mỗi-phiên, nhường-nhịn lúc `init`, manifest `.fgos/coexistence.json`, Known Gaps chưa flip; `src/install/coexist.mjs` — cài đặt detection + manifest (read-only, không đè)
- `package.json` (`version`, `files`, `bin.fgos`, `bin.fgos-runner`) + `README.md` (mục `## Install`) — cài `fgos` VÀ `fgos-runner` từ ngoài source repo qua GitHub install, cả hai executable ngay sau cài; `test/install-packaging.test.mjs` — proof e2e (pack → install → chạy từ project ngoài, gồm cả hai binary); spec: docs/specs/distribution.md

sourceBindings.sourceContent:
- **RUL77 ([ĐÃ BỊ THAY phần "each door carries one posture lane" bởi RUL90 (the raw dispatch doors are removed), decision 0062 — posture now comes from the Unit's `writes` plus the capability; "an agent executor declares no `for`" stands] posture belongs to the capability, an agent executor declares no `for`, and each door carries one posture lane; supersedes RUL76 (`execute --for ` with a "must declare" gate), 2026-10-13).** An agent executor can do any kind of work, so no `for` list describes it, and a list on one was read as the posture of every dispatch to it (`docs/specs/confinement-authority.md` already said a direct executor call must carry a capability anchor and never infer the minimum from `executor.for`). `resolveCapabilityDetailsFromHints` reads `for` from tool executors only; on an agent executor it is inert (config still loads, so projects and worktrees that carry one keep dispatching) and `fgos doctor` names it under `executor-profile-warnings` (`executor..agent-for-inert`); the agent executors' `for` lists are gone from this repo's `.fgos/config.json` (`decide --for` routing unchanged: it reads `capabilities..prefer`). The CLI door `execute ` refuses before spawning when no `--for` is given (`capability-required`, listing the writing capabilities and the read-only door); programmatic callers (Assignment, Work) pass their own capability hints and are unchanged. `execute --for ` runs the invocation that capability `prefer`s for that executor, else the first plain cli invocation with no sandbox backend, instead of always the first cli invocation. That door leases no provider account, so it carries writing work only: a capability with required confinement is refused (`posture-needs-assignment`). Read-only work runs sandboxed as a Workflow unit with `writes: []` (`fgos workflow start --units`), which binds the read-only posture and leases the account (the architecture-advisory seats ran that way: `confined-bwrap`, login provisioned); `execute --contract --executor ` keeps a named provider and leases its account but runs unconfined, read-only by instruction only (measured: `execute openai --for code:review` on the bare door ran `codex-cli-bwrap` confined and got 401 with no login; the same read through `--contract --executor openai` answered, on `cli-spawn` with `confinement: null`). A sandboxed read-only door that also keeps a named provider does not exist yet. The calling agent answers Q1 (does it write? does a provider matter?) from prose doctrine in `core/skills/_shared/capability-matching.md`, with no classifier or workflow generator. Decided after an `architecture-advisory` run (`wf-run-1791875339761-10315b91`: framing and shaping with three blind seats and a synthesizer completed; critique was blocked by a Codex trust prompt, so no reviewed synthesis exists). Not built: a soft provider hint on `decide` (`--prefer`, the synthesizer's recommendation) — naming the executor on `execute` already lets a caller pick a provider, and the hint would change `bind()`, shared with Workflow binding; revisit when a caller needs "this provider if it can, else any". Since 2026-10-14 (RUL88 (ad-hoc Unit prefer and persona, the one-liner), decision 0061) that hint exists on the Unit, not on `decide`: `fgos run "" --provider ` and an ad-hoc Unit's `prefer` try the provider first and fail over into the pool, and a read-only one-liner is the sandboxed read-only door that keeps a preferred provider. 1. **Account lock.** One kernel mutex per provider account, machine scope, at `/locks/provider-account//.lock` through holder-lock, separate from the state lock (`provider-state.lock`). A waiter waits with timers, never by blocking the event loop (panel seats share a process and may share an account); a caller that must not wait (a removal) tries once. The renewal or unlock-probe call runs through the lock (`spawnHolding`, i.e. `runBorrowed`), so a dead holder with a live call keeps the lock and a second renewal never redeems the same refresh token; the lock is released only after the call and every process it started have exited. The account directory `/account-locks///` still holds the pending copies, the scratch home and the cooldown. 2. **Refresh-ahead.** After the final account selection (the executor-fallback lease included) and before a confined private home is built from it, when the login has less than the window left, fgOS renews it once. The window is `max(60 minutes, probe timeout + 5 minutes)`. Only the entry of the dispatched provider counts, for the window and for "was it renewed" (Codex: its single entry; pi: the key equal to the provider id or starting with `-`; omp: the row `provider` likewise; a lone oauth entry of another provider is not used; zero or several matches skip the renewal as `entry-unidentified`), so an abandoned login of another provider never makes every dispatch renew, and only that entry is made due and applied. Under the account lock it applies any leftover copy first, re-reads the source, and skips for 30 minutes after a failed renewal; then it builds a scratch home under the account directory (mode 0700, the listed files only), makes only that copy look due, runs the layout's probe call on it (wrapped in coreutils `timeout --kill-after=5`, so the child ends on its own even if the runner dies and the account lock does not outlive it unbounded; the runner's own timer stays; the lazy-probe unlock call, an account locked for a dead login, is wrapped the same way), and applies the renewed entry to the real store. The real store is never made to look expired, so the owner's own CLI does not renew because of this, a failed or hung call leaves it untouched, and a scratch copy left by a dead runner is applied (if newer) by the next lock holder and then removed. Where each layout keeps its expiry: pi `auth.json` `.expires` (ms; seconds below 1e12), `type: oauth` entries only; omp `agent.db` table `auth_credentials`, `data.expires` (ms), rows `credential_type = 'oauth'` and no `disabled_cause`; Codex `auth.json`, due at the earlier of the access token's `exp` claim and `last_refresh` plus 8 days (`TOKEN_REFRESH_INTERVAL`, `should_refresh_proactively` in `codex-rs/login/src/auth/manager.rs` of openai/codex; the same file renews at five minutes before `exp` when the token can be read). A layout that cannot be read (an API key, agy, no `node:sqlite`) is left as it was. 3. **Apply (compare-before-write).** Shared by refresh-ahead and write-back, always under the account lock: only an entry whose expiry is strictly later than the source's and whose refresh token differs from the source's replaces it (compared in memory, never printed; a copy that still holds the source's refresh token renewed nothing), and for a fresh renewal the new expiry must also be in the future, while a copy staged earlier (a pane's home, a pending or leftover copy) is applied even if its access token has expired since, because its refresh token is the newer one and the source's is already spent, only that entry changes (other pi providers, other omp rows and columns, other Codex fields stay as they were), a copy that cannot be read, has an unexpected shape, or has no refresh token where the source's entry has one never touches the source. A copy is deleted only when the source was read successfully and proves the copy is not newer (same refresh token, or an expiry not strictly later), or when the copy is proven malformed (corrupt JSON, or it parses to no usable entry, or it has no store file); when the source is unreadable or half-written, the entry cannot be identified at apply time, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass (`node:sqlite` unavailable, a database that will not open), the copy is kept (a fresh scratch copy moves to `pending/`) and the result is `apply-deferred`, never `applied` or `not-renewed`. An operating-system read error on a copy file (permissions, I/O) is reported as `unreadable-file` and keeps the copy (`apply-deferred`); only a store file that is not there (`missing-file`) is proven empty. pi and Codex files are replaced through a temp file and a rename, recomputed when the source changed in between; the omp store is changed by a row update in one transaction, never by replacing the file the owner's omp may hold open. 4. **Write-back at removal.** When a dispatch opted in, the private home's ownership marker records `credentialWriteBack` (provider, account, source home, layout, runtime dir; names and paths only). One removal function serves the driver cleanup, the finalizer of a settled dispatch and the orphan reaper: before deleting a home whose marker asks for it, a login in the home that is newer than the source's is staged under `pending/` (atomic rename) and applied under the account lock, tried once without waiting; when the lock is busy, or nothing proves the copy is not newer (the source is unreadable, its entry cannot be identified, or the copy cannot be read for a reason that may pass, such as `node:sqlite` being unavailable: an omp store is then staged as plain files, write-ahead log included), it stays pending and the next refresh-ahead (or removal) applies it once it can be identified, even if the source still looks fresh, because the source's own refresh token may already be spent; a refresh-ahead that skips because the entry is unidentified applies the pending copies too, so the ones that have become identifiable clear. Pending copies are limited to five per login store (per account for a single-store account, per `stores/` for a per-CLI one), but only redundant ones are ever dropped: after the pending copies were applied, under the account lock, a copy whose logins are identical to another pending copy's (compared in memory by entry key, refresh token and expiry, or by the bytes of the store files and of a non-empty write-ahead log or rollback journal when a copy cannot be parsed; never printed) is dropped, oldest first, while the account is over the limit, and the newest of each identical group stays; a drop writes one stderr line `credential-pending-dropped` with a count only. A copy that cannot be shown redundant, or obsolete by the source, is never dropped to make room, so an account can stay over the limit, and the doctor check reports it. A staged copy and the pending directory are synced to disk before the home goes. A copy a probe left half-written (pi rewrites its store in place; omp commits row updates in a database transaction) is kept under `torn/` for hand recovery, never applied or dropped automatically, and reported by the doctor check at any age. This covers the probe's scratch copy only: a scratch home a dead runner left, and a pane home whose store was cut off, are still removed when their JSON cannot be read. A pane home whose store files are byte for byte the source's, with no non-empty write-ahead log or rollback journal on either side (a login renewed before a checkpoint sits only there; a zero-byte or missing one counts as none, the shared-memory index counts for nothing, and one that cannot be read, other than as missing, is never taken for none), renewed nothing and is not staged, parsable or not. If staging itself fails, the private home and its marker are kept (the removal reports failure, one stderr line with a fixed code and no path or value) so a later removal, the reaper's included, retries; only a copy proven malformed, or one the source was read to prove not newer, lets the home go. Each failed attempt is counted in the marker (`credentialKept`: attempts, first time, time of the last counted attempt; failures less than 15 minutes after the last counted one are not counted again, so a transient fault does not use the budget up); the marker is rewritten through a temp file and a rename, and a marker that is present but unreadable stops the removal. After five attempts the home is held: no further removal attempt and no deletion by age, however old. A held home is re-checked, under the account lock, when that account is next renewed (the temp roots searched are the same as doctor's: the default one plus each registered backend's own `tempRoot`; a home under a backend's separate `privateHomeRoot` is in none of them, so no check, repair, reaper or renewal sees it, and it is never deleted either) and by `fgos doctor --fix`, and only a home of the lock's own runtime directory: it is removed only when the source is readable and proves its login is not newer, or when that login can now be staged beside the source (and is applied); otherwise it stays held. A marker file that is no recognisable marker at all (not JSON, not an object, no contract name) stops any removal of its home. The finalizer compares the ownership marker's digest without `credentialKept` (a failed driver cleanup adds it after the digest was taken) and carries on with the dispatch's other resources past a home that cannot go (the dispatch is recorded as retained, with the home's reason). The doctor check `credential-copies-retained` reports, by provider and account, held homes (a failure, naming the home directory), homes still being retried and pending or scratch copies older than a day (warnings), with counts, ages and never a value; the check deletes nothing. Any other write-back problem is reported on stderr by a fixed code and never stops the removal. 5. **Known exposure.** Refresh-ahead can spend the refresh token that a pane started just outside the window still holds: that pane's own renewal is then refused, no worse than before this rule, and write-back cannot rescue it because its renewal failed. A run that copied the login with more than the window left and runs longer than that remainder is the case. 6. **No value in any output.** Results, events, markers, cooldown and lock records, stderr and reports carry fixed codes (`unreadable-json`, `unexpected-shape`, `sqlite-unavailable`, ...) and fingerprints at most, never a token or a parser message (which quotes nearby input). - **RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store, 2026-10-13).** A herdr pane with a private home carries the login of the account the capacity layer leased (RUL65b), but the folder-trust seed (`seedWorkspaceTrust`, `trustStorePaths` in `src/runner/dispatch/herdr-round.mjs`) derived the trust decision from the store of the account the invocation's static env names (`codex-herdr-fgovn`: `CODEX_HOME=${HOME}/.codex-fgovn`). When the two accounts differ and the static one was never asked about the repo, the seed refused (`untrusted-root`) and Codex stopped at "Trust this folder?" (measured 2026-10-13 14:24, run `unit-run-1791876207053-efe6686b/reviewer/1/runs/01`: the leased `tetcu72` trusts `/home/vantt/projects/forgentX`, `~/.codex-fgovn/config.toml` did not; reproduced read-only with a scratch static home: the main-branch code blocked on herdr rule `trust_directory`, the fixed code settled confined). Now the leased credential source travels with the dispatch (`executeThroughConfinement` adapter option `trustAccountSource` -> herdr-spawn adapter -> the round), and for a round with its own private home the decision is read from that account's store: a `codex-home` source's `config.toml`, a `home-files` source's agy settings. A declared `trustStore.path` still wins; a round without a private home still reads the invocation's home, because that is what its CLI reads. Codex hook trust, seeded from the same root, follows. The "trust vanishing" of 2026-10-07 (another Codex session rewriting an account `config.toml`) is a separate cause this does not remove: it still bites when the leased account's own entry is lost. Not proven: whether Codex 0.160 honours trust given to an ancestor directory (`/home/vantt/projects`); the seed still requires the repo root itself. - **RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment, diagnostic only, 2026-10-13).** A dispatch failure on one CLI does not say whether the account (dead login, quota) or the CLI (trust prompt, sandbox, version bug) is at fault. `fgos dispatch probe-account --provider

--account [--executor ] [--invocation ] [--timeout-ms ]` (`src/runner/dispatch/provider-account-probe.mjs`) starts every invocation that runs as the account at once through the Assignment door a Workflow unit uses (read-only posture binding, invocation pinned by `cliOverride`, inventory narrowed to the one account so the lease cannot pick another and a quarantine still refuses, RUL75 (a rotating login is renewed once at the source and written back from a private home) renewal opt-in), with a trivial prompt, and reports per CLI an outcome class (`ok`, `blocked-trust-prompt`, `auth`, `quota`, `sandbox`, `timeout`, `other`), the evidence line, the assignment, run directory and pane, plus a verdict (`healthy`; `account-fault` when every CLI failed with `auth`/`quota`; `cli-fault` when one answered; `mixed`; `no-confined-cli` when no probed invocation declares a sandbox). The verdict reads only the rows whose invocation declares its own sandbox (`confined: true`, each row's `inVerdict`): the read-only posture makes the door confine every round (`resolvePosture` returns a required `host-write-denied` requirement), and an invocation that declares no sandbox binds no private home either, so its CLI meets its own login directory (`CODEX_HOME`, `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR`) mounted read-only and stops on `EROFS` before it answers. That row is still run and reported (outcome `sandbox`, truthfully: a read-only dispatch pinned to that invocation fails the same way), but it says nothing about the account or the CLI (2026-10-13: tetcu72, fgovn and tetnu answered on every sandboxed invocation while `pi-cli-` and `codex-cli-bypass-fgovn` died on `EROFS` under `local-bwrap-v1`, and the verdict read `cli-fault`). An invocation runs as the account when it is confined with a private home whose CLI the account's credential layout logs in (`lease`), when its credential env names the account home (`env`), or when its id ends with `-` (`name`, the config's `--` convention). It closes the panes the rounds left open and removes the private homes kept for them; it picks and schedules nothing. First real run (openai/tetcu72): both Codex invocations `ok` (cli-spawn under bwrap and the herdr pane), both pi invocations `sandbox` (`EROFS` on `~/.pi/accounts/openai-tetcu72/settings.json.lock`: under the read-only posture pi cannot write its own account directory, which it does before answering; outside confinement the same pi account answered), verdict `cli-fault`. - **RUL80 (an account is chosen first, then a CLI: one login store per CLI, quota and locks per account, 2026-10-13).** One provider account may be used through several CLIs (Codex, pi, omp), and each CLI keeps its own login store, so an account declared with a single `credentialSource` gave every confined CLI the one store (openai `tetcu72` declared its Codex home, so its confined pi invocations got a Codex login and pi failed on its own directory, RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment)). An account in the machine-global inventory now declares exactly one of `credentialSource` (one store, used for every CLI, unchanged; other projects use it) or `credentialSources` (`{ : }`, the key is the store key an invocation declares in `credentialStore.use` (RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads)): `codex`, `pi`, `omp`, `agy`; each source has the same `kind`/`home`/`files` shape). Every reader takes the store of the CLI actually dispatched: the confinement request (`buildConfinementRequest`) resolves `providerCapacity.credentialSource` from the invocation's store key, so private-home provisioning, the write-back marker and the folder-trust seed (RUL78 (a confined pane reads its folder trust from the leased account's own store)) see that store, and a CLI the leased account has no store for is refused before the worker starts (`credential-provisioning`). The lease does not know the invocation unless it is pinned (`cliOverride.preferInvocation`, as Workflow units and the account probe pin it): a pinned lease only picks an account that has a store for the pinned CLI (`provider-capacity.no-account-for-cli` when none has); an unpinned lease picks among all accounts as before. *(Superseded by RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine per pool): the lease now receives the CLI from the launched invocation's declared login store, pinned or not, so an account with no store for that CLI is never leased.)* Refresh-ahead (RUL75 (a rotating login is renewed once at the source and written back from a private home)) runs before the invocation is settled, so for a per-CLI account it renews the store of each CLI the executor may still launch (the pinned one only, when pinned); the lazy unlock probe (RUL74 (an account locked for a dead login unlocks itself after one real call)) calls through the store of the first such CLI. Renewal copies of a per-CLI store wait under `account-locks///stores//` (`pending/`, scratch homes, cooldown), never beside another store's copies, and the marker records the store; the account lock stays one per account, and `credential-copies-retained` reads both places. A copy left where the account's current layout does not read (the account directory after the account moved to one store per CLI, `stores/` after it went back to one store or dropped that CLI, or an account the inventory no longer lists) is never applied, moved to the new layout or dropped: when the machine-global inventory was read, the check fails on it at any age (a torn copy and an over-limit pending directory there included) and names that directory for hand recovery; when the global config cannot be read or is refused by the validator, the check fails instead, names the reason (an error class and the config path, never the parser's own text), lists every retained copy at any age and promises nothing about a dispatch, since a dispatch could not run on that config either. Quota, leases, quarantine and rotation stay per account: no account is split into pseudo-accounts per CLI. The account probe (RUL79 (`fgos dispatch probe-account`: one account, every CLI, at the same moment)) leases an account into each confined CLI it has a store for. `confined-pane-accounts` in `fgos doctor` checks each confined invocation that reads a store against the store it names (RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads)). An fgos release from before this rule refuses an inventory that uses `credentialSources` (unknown account key), so the inventory is changed only after the release that reads it is active. The same store directory also holds `torn/` (a login store a probe left half-written, kept for hand recovery and never applied or dropped), and a crash during staging can leave `pending/.tmp--`: `credential-copies-retained` reports it once its writer process is gone and it has not changed for ten minutes, and `fgos doctor --fix` removes one only after claiming it by rename (so a writer that is still running loses its own rename and keeps its home) and only when it is empty, has the same files as a copy the store keeps in `pending/` or `torn/` (the shared-memory index aside), or, under the account lock, the source login of the account shows it is no newer or it is malformed; never by age, and any other stays for hand recovery. The bwrap driver points `env[homeEnv]` at the private home (over a value the invocation's own `env` carries, which names the real store) and copies the files of the store: the invocation's `files`, else the leased account's list (`home-files`), else `auth.json` (`codex-home`). **The copy rule replaces "a missing file refuses the launch":** files that are present are copied, an absent one is left out, and a store with none present refuses the launch with `credential-provisioning` (`credential-store-empty`, naming the account, the store key and the home); a dangling link, a link out of the home, a non-regular file or a path with `..` still refuses, as before. **An invocation that declares no store gets no login and no home variable, whatever account was leased** (the lesson of `569f72d3b`, which copied a Codex login into every executor's home), and `assessBwrap` refuses a policy that grants no `private-home` to an invocation that reads a store. Trust seeding, write-back and refresh-ahead keep reading the leased account's store, now chosen by the store key. `dispatch explain` names the store of the bound invocation and whether it is declared or inferred; `fgos doctor` `confined-pane-accounts` (same id) covers every confined invocation that reads a store, notes absent files and fails only when none is present. In this repo's committed config the invocations of one CLI under one executor collapse into one (`pi-cli-bwrap`; the account is leased at launch), invocation ids no longer carry an account name (`codex-herdr`, `omp-herdr`, `omp-cli-bwrap`), and the OpenRouter key variable left the pi `env` because pi reads the key from the store's `auth.json` (measured 2026-10-19: with the key variables unset and only the three store files, pi answered). Not changed: leasing, quarantine, `llmAccounts`, the account inventory shape; the leased account is still chosen before the invocation is known, so an account that has no file of the store fails late (B1 filters accounts by store key before the lease), and the older fields stay in the committed config until the release that reads `credentialStore` is active. - **RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order and its cell entries; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine are per pool; a missing cell refuses by name, 2026-10-20).** Owner decisions 2026-10-19 (plan `261019-2312-model-pool-b1-fallback-and-account-order`), the walk of RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool)'s cells made real. **Candidates.** `bind()` expands each `prefer` executor into one candidate per entry of its family's cell at the seat's tier (RUL102 (a tier cell names its pool)), in cell order: `{ executor, invocation, pool, model }`; an entry without `@` is the family-named pool. `provenance.model.source` reads `modelPolicies..[]` (it read `resolveTierModel(.)`). `resolveTierModel` is the model of the cell's first entry whichever pool serves it (the legacy dispatch path, the runner dry-run and doctor name that model; it no longer refuses a cell that names only other pools), and `supportsPolicyTier` is true for any cell with an entry. A seat that leases an account (an out-of-process agent that is not a tool) needs the cell; an in-process, inline or tool seat needs none and binds with `pool: null`. **Primary.** The first binding follows `prefer` order exactly as before, with the soft family spread of the panel seats unchanged, so council seats keep leading with different families. **After a failure** the walk takes, in order: the failed family's remaining cell entries, then the families `runner.tierFallback.` lists, limited to the families `prefer` names (a list narrows and never widens); with no list for the tier, the rest of the `prefer` order after the failed candidate. A walk never leaves its tier. The soft spread stays active in a walk and ranks the passing candidates, ties falling to walk order; without a spread request the walk takes the first untried candidate. **`runner.tierFallback`** is `{ : [family, ...] }` with the tiers of `modelPolicies`, each a non-empty list of distinct family names (the `modelPolicies` key, so GLM is `z-ai`); `validateTierFallbackShape` refuses anything else at load naming the key path, `tierFallbackOf` reads it, and doctor `tier-fallback` warns on a listed family with no cell at that tier or no agent executor. The code enforces the tier boundary and the narrowing only; the owner's groups are configuration: doer tiers (nano, standard, advanced) fall back across gemini, deepseek, z-ai, then claude, openai; flagship and frontier across claude, openai, gemini and xai. An older release ignores the unknown runner key, so the lists go in the project config. **Walk state** is the seat's earlier bindings (`tried`, identity = executor, invocation, pool and model), rebuilt from the attempts in `unit.json` by `triedBindingsOf`; `excludePools` replaces `excludeFamilies`: a dead login excludes that pool, not the family's other pools (RUL106 (a seat walks a tier's declared order; accounts rotate in declared order; lease, state and quarantine per pool) supersedes the walk of 0058 items 2 to 3 and 6, and the `candidateIndex` chain of 0051 item 1). A retry on another account of the same candidate is not a step of the walk. `walkStateOf` is the one door that turns a recorded attempt into those two `bind()` options; the write gate and doctor `mutating-assignment-binding-snapshot` both recompute through it, so a fallback attempt (`-fb`) is checked against the walk it was bound in. The write gate compares executor, pool, tier and posture. A unit record written before bindings carried a pool has no walk state this code reads: its bindings are left out and the walk restarts at the primary. **A pool is usable** when the lease can serve it: a pool with accounts needs an enabled account holding a login store for the CLI the chosen invocation declares (`credentialStore.use`, RUL105 (an invocation declares the login store it reads)); a pool with no account in either inventory is usable only as the family-named pool (the executor's own login). This reads config only (`poolUnusableReason`), so `bind()` stays pure; quarantine and leases are the lease's business at dispatch. An unusable entry is out of the candidates with `pool-unusable`, and `fgos dispatch explain` says why. **Missing cell.** An out-of-process agent seat whose family has no cell at the tier it runs at refuses `tier-cell-missing`: `no model for tier "" under family "" (runner.modelPolicies..)`, one text built by `tierCellMissingDetail` for `bind()` and for the assignment policy (which raises `tier-cell-missing: `). The older fallthrough to `executor.model` or the CLI default is deleted. When several `prefer` families exist, or in a walk, a family with no cell is skipped and recorded in `provenance.skipped`, and the refusal names the last skipped cell when nothing is left; a lone candidate refuses at once. **Lease, state and quarantine are per pool.** A seat bound to a pool leases from it: the state key is `legacyStateKey(pool)`, so the family-named pool keeps the key it always had (`openai` is `openai-codex`) and existing state, sticky records and quarantines still apply; a quarantine or fault on one pool does not touch another pool of the same family. The accounts of a pool come from `runner.llmAccounts.` when it declares the pool, else from `runner.providers..accounts`: **the transition read** (`providerAccountInventory`), which goes, together with the `runner.providers` key, once every fgOS release on the machine reads `runner.llmAccounts` (the later step that deletes `runner.providers` from the global config). `compareWithLegacyInventory` and doctor `llm-accounts-vs-legacy` go with it. **Account order is the declared order.** `rankProviderAccounts` takes the account the assignment already holds while it is usable, else the pool's accounts in the key order of the config, skipping quarantined and `disabled` ones; load does not reorder, so the first account takes every lease until it cannot (least-lease and least-recently-used are deleted from the ranking; `lastSelectedAt` is still written for `inspect`). An account id of digits only is refused (a JS object lists such a key first and would reorder the list). The lease receives the CLI from the launched invocation's declared login store (the pinned invocation, else the executor's first `cli` invocation), and `inspectAccountRotation` counts the enabled accounts of the pool for rotation. **Pin.** `--account` and the `account` key of `--override` take `pool/account` (`parseAccountPin`); a bare id is refused with the form to write. The pin selects the candidate of the chosen family whose pool matches; otherwise the seat binds unpinned and `provenance.account.skipped` names why (`account-pin-other-pool`, `account-pin-no-inventory`, `account-pin-unsupported`); an unknown account of the seat's own pool refuses `account-pin-unknown` and a disabled one `account-pin-disabled`. `binding.account` is `{ pool, id }`. `fgos workflow start --account` takes the same form and checks it against the pool's inventory at start. **Reversal triggers.** (3) Declared order goes back to least-lease ranking if one account keeps hitting its quota window while others sit idle (watch: `fgos dispatch inspect --provider-capacity` shows `openLeases` and quarantines per account). (2) The tier groups change when a family's model at a tier stops being equivalent in price or quality. Primary order stays `prefer`: if one family keeps failing first for a capability, narrow its `prefer` rather than reorder primaries globally. **Not changed.** `attemptProviderCapacityFallback` (the legacy dispatch path and workflow operations that declare `policy.fallbackExecutors`) is a second walker that leases by family key without the CLI and does not use the walk; the write gate recomputes without `independentOf` and `preferIndependentOf`, so a spread-chosen primary can differ from the recompute; per-capability tier ceilings and spend tracking are not built. Component boundary: no change (`bind()` decides candidates, the lease decides accounts). - Phần chọn ghế của rule này bị D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding: one authority for agent seat choice) thay một phần, 2026-10-20: authority đích là [seat-binding.md](seat-binding.md); code đổi cùng plan của nó. Chữ rule ở trên không sửa tại chỗ. - **(herdr panes open through terminal-control, 2026-10-18; the round itself moved to the run supervisor, same day).** A herdr seat no longer has a round loop in the controller: the controller prepares the attempt (brief, home, trust seed, `allocate(key = attempt id, groupKey)`), writes a `terminal`-mode envelope and hands it to the run supervisor, which opens, briefs, watches and releases the pane through `fgos-terminal-control` (`docs/platform/run-supervisor/spec.md` section 5.3, `docs/platform/terminal-control/spec.md`). The group key is the dispatch batch key, else the unit run id, so every attempt of one batch lands in one tab; `FGOS_HERDR_ANCHOR_PANE` is an `attach` into that group. A failed or stopped attempt's pane is kept until a person closes it (a positive `terminal.retainFailedPaneMs` only makes doctor report the pane with its pane id once that time has passed; nothing closes it) and a finished one is closed once by `release-slot`; `terminal.layout.*` and `terminal.allocationGraceMs` reach the route from the project (then global) config, and doctor's `terminal-control` and `terminal-allocations` checks show what an attempt would use. Starting a herdr server for a confined session stays in `worker-session-boot.mjs` (a server lifecycle, not a pane operation). - **(a private home belongs to its attempt, 2026-10-18; ends the confinement orphan reaper).** Only adopt's finalize-home step removes the private home of an attempt, while the attempt lock is free and its process domain is empty; the sweep (`sweepAttempts`) is adopt alone. The pane, binder and expiry rules, `bind`/`markLaunched`/`retain`, the post-probe sweep and the herdr-launch-command write are removed; a herdr-spawn launch needs an attempt id. Why: the old rules judged a home by a pid, a pane or an age, which could take the home of a worker still running (S2); one owner removes that class of fault. Left open: a dispatch outside the assignment door that dies leaves its home (named by `fgos doctor`, removed only by an explicit `doctor --fix`, never swept), and `fgos run` no longer has a startup rule for homes written with a pane binding by an older release. - **(a Unit carries its own verify and skills, verify runs bounded, and a reviewed run at rigor high or critical needs a family per seat, 2026-10-18; owner decisions 2026-10-18; the rigor part supersedes decision 0055 for `reviewed` only).** - **`verify` stays on the Unit.** `validateUnit` keeps `verify` (a non-empty shell command) and `skills` (a non-empty list of skill names, trimmed, de-duplicated) through validation, the units-file loader, the workflow template and the round; a registered workflow template may set both too. - **Where the verify command comes from.** `verifyCommandOf` (`patterns/reviewed.mjs`) reads the Unit's own `verify`, else its capability's `verify`, and nothing else; the `code-change` preset pins none (it used to name `npm test`, which no runner ever executed, so a reviewed run recorded a verify pass that checked nothing), and `params.verify` no longer counts. A reviewed run with no verify command still passes on its checkers but its result carries `verify: { ran: false, reason }`; a solo or panel run, which has no verify step, says nothing. - **One bounded runner.** The verify step runs through `runCommand` (`src/runner/goal-check.mjs`, the same runner `return` and `approve` use) in the Unit's worktree, for at most `runner.timeoutMs` (the existing key and default; no new key, so nothing new for setup or doctor to register). A non-zero exit, a command that could not start and one that ran past the limit are each a failed verify that becomes findings naming the status (`exited N`, `timed out after Nms`, `could not run`) and the last twenty lines of output; none of them hangs the run. - **One-liner flags.** `fgos run "" --input , --verify ""` set the Unit's `inputs` and `verify`; both are refused beside `--unit` or `--resume`, and an empty value is refused before any unit run exists. - **Skills reach `bind()`.** `bind()` skips an executor whose `supports.skills` (new optional key in the executor's `supports` block, a non-empty array of names) does not list every skill the Unit names; none left refuses with reason `skills-unavailable` naming the missing skills, and the session lead never takes over such a Unit inline. Only roles that do the Unit's work are asked for skills: checker, panel and debate roles (`reviewer`, `red-team`, `tester`, `panelist*`, `synthesizer`, `thesis`, `antithesis`, `judge`) are chosen on independence alone. An executor that declares no `supports.skills` provides none. `fgos doctor` check `executor-skills-installed` fails when a declared skill has no `SKILL.md` in its runtime's skill directory of the main checkout (by each invocation's CLI: `claude` reads `.claude/skills/`, `codex` `.agents/skills/`, `omp` `.omp/skills/`, `pi` `.pi/skills/`, `grok` `.grok/skills/`, and an executor passes only when every invocation's directory has the skill; `ak:cook` is the directory `ak-cook`); `worktreeSetup.commands` copies the untracked `ak-*` skill directories from the main checkout into each new worktree, so a worker sees them. `fgos worktree create` records what its provisioning placed (`provisionWorktree` in `src/runner/worktree.mjs`: every new untracked or ignored path, with a content digest for a file and the target for a symlink, and the `node_modules` it installed declared regenerable) in `/worktree-provisioning/.json`, bound to the checkout directory's device and inode. `fgos worktree remove` moves exactly those bytes into a sibling directory before the Git port's clean check (`setProvisionedAside`): a copy only while it still matches its digest, and a recorded directory only once it is empty. It moves them back when the port refuses and deletes them, with the record, once the port has removed the checkout. A worker-edited copy or any byte the record does not name stays in place, and the port refuses on it. The brief for an `ak:cook` worker is `core/skills/_shared/ak-cook-worker-contract.md`. - **`docs:write`** is a curated capability slot (`DEFAULT_CAPABILITY_SLOTS`, description-only, `serves: { outputKind: change, domain: docs, mutates: true }`) next to `code:implement`, so `fgos setup` declares the capability the one-liner and `fgos-run` name for documentation work. - **Rigor high or critical: every seat of a `reviewed` run on its own family.** When the Unit's rigor, or its capability's rigor floor (the stronger of the two, as `bind()` computes it), is `high` or `critical`, each checker is `independentOf` the producer and of every other checker (`requiresDistinctFamilies`), a fallback walk after a provider limit re-reads that list so the replacement keeps the property, and a pool without enough families refuses the seat that cannot be placed with the existing reason `independence`. Standard and low keep the old rule (checker differs from the producer only). Decision 0055's soft spread is unchanged for `panel`: seat count there is still not capped by family count (owner, 2026-10-11). - **`debate`: two sides soft, the judge hard.** `runDebate` (`patterns/debate.mjs`) dispatches `thesis` and `antithesis` read-only with `preferIndependentOf` each other (a shared family is reported, not refused), optionally a second round where each side gets only the other's round-1 result in `inputs`, then `judge` with `independentOf: [thesis, antithesis]` and every result as `inputs`. The judge's family differing from both sides is the one hard independence rule of the pattern; an unseatable judge is bind()'s named `independence` refusal (`policy-refusal` outcome), never a same-family ruling. The three roles are listed once, in `CHECKER_ROLES` of `bind.mjs`, so they never run inline or in-process and are not asked for the Unit's skills. `fgos doctor`'s pool-independence check drives the same pattern code, so a pool with too few families fails it before a run. `unit-summary` gives the sides seat kind `producer` and the judge `judge`.
